summaries.gardner: NetEase fits Gardner's Rule Breaker approach only partly. It is a founder-led maker of hit games with global breakouts such as Marvel Rivals, but it is the number-two player in a maturing Chinese game market rather than the leader of a new industry, and its ADSs fell 14.6% over the past 52 weeks while analysts mostly rate it a buy.
summaries.buffett: NetEase has several Buffett-style traits: a long profit record, a 64.3% gross margin and 30% net margin in 2025, operating cash flow of RMB50.7B and net cash of RMB167.5B at June 2026, with founder William Ding owning a large stake. Against that, each new game is a bet on creative success, and Chinese regulation and the VIE structure make its future earnings harder to predict than Buffett usually likes.
summaries.munger: Munger would like the cash-rich, high-return business and an owner-operator founder, and the price (about 17 times trailing earnings) is not demanding for a business of this quality. Thinking backwards, the main ways it could fail are a run of failed games, Chinese government action (as in the December 2023 draft spending rules) and US-China tensions affecting the ADSs.
summaries.lynch: Lynch would most likely call NetEase a stalwart: revenue grew every year from RMB73.7B in 2020 to RMB112.6B in 2025 but only 7.0% in 2025, with consensus calling for about 7% a year ahead. Its trailing P/E of about 17 is well above that growth rate, so it fails his PEG test, though the 2.3% dividend yield and large net cash soften this.
summaries.fisher: NetEase fits many of Fisher's points: it keeps launching new products (Eggy Party, Marvel Rivals, Where Winds Meet), its RMB17.7B of R&D in 2025 has produced hits, and margins have risen steadily (operating margin from 18.7% in 2021 to 31.8% in 2025). Weaker points are its reliance on a handful of franchises and limited disclosure typical of Chinese companies.
summaries.graham: NetEase passes Graham's tests for size, financial strength and a long profit record, and diluted earnings per ADS rose roughly fivefold from 2015 to 2025. It fails on valuation (P/E of about 17 times P/B of 3.2 is about 55, far above 22.5; about 17.8 times three-year average earnings) and on a 20-year unbroken dividend record.
summaries.thiel: On Thiel's questions NetEase scores moderately: it has deep, hard-to-copy game-making know-how and long-lived franchises, but no technology ten times better than Tencent's or miHoYo's, and no monopoly in its markets. Its strongest answers are on team (a founder who has run it since 1997) and durability of its biggest franchises.
summaries.gerstner: Gerstner would see a profitable, cash-rich company trading at about 13 times forward earnings with a 9.3% free-cash-flow yield, which fits his focus on efficiency and fair valuation. Growth of about 7% a year and limited exposure to the AI platform shift make it a less obvious fit for his growth and AI-focused portfolio.
summaries.druckenmiller: Druckenmiller looks for earnings acceleration and favourable liquidity and price trends. NetEase's operating profit rose 33.4% year on year in Q2 2026, but the shares fell 14.6% over the past 52 weeks and the stock depends on Chinese policy and US-China relations, so the setup is mixed rather than compelling.
summaries.smith: NetEase matches much of Terry Smith's approach: high gross margins (64.3% in 2025), high returns on equity (about 20% while holding huge net cash), strong cash conversion and little debt. Smith would worry that hit-driven games are less predictable than consumer staples-style franchises, but the price (about 10.7 times free cash flow) does not look like overpaying.
summaries.greenblatt: NetEase scores well on the Magic Formula: EV/EBIT is about 9.6 (an earnings yield of about 10%) because net cash makes up roughly a quarter of its market value, and its return on tangible capital is very high. This makes it the kind of good-and-cheap stock Greenblatt's screen favours.
summaries.akre: On Akre's three-legged stool NetEase is strong on the business (high returns, high margins) and on the owner-operator leg (founder William Ding owns a large stake), but weaker on reinvestment: it generates far more cash than it can reinvest, returning it through dividends and buybacks and piling up net cash.
summaries.pabrai: Pabrai likes simple, cash-rich businesses bought at low prices with little downside. NetEase's large net cash (RMB167.5B, about 30% of its market value), steady profits and roughly 13 times forward earnings limit downside, but it is not in a temporary distressed situation that would create a classic Dhandho bargain.
summaries.wood: NetEase is a weak fit for Cathie Wood's disruptive-innovation focus. It uses AI in its games and in Youdao's learning tools, but it is not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or genomics, and its markets grow in single digits.
summaries.ackman: NetEase meets several of Ackman's criteria: a simple, predictable-ish, free-cash-flow-generating business with high margins, a fortress balance sheet and a dominant position in its niche. The VIE structure, dependence on new hits and Chinese regulatory risk reduce the predictability he insists on.
summaries.sleep: Nick Sleep looked for scale economies shared with customers and long reinvestment runways. NetEase's free-to-play model and long-lived games give players lasting value, but its growing scale is not clearly passed back to customers in a way that compounds a lasting advantage, so the fit is partial.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge, fast-growing markets and products solving painful problems. NetEase is a mature, profitable game maker in a large but slow-growing market, so it fits his venture approach poorly, though its record of hit-making shows strong product teams.
summaries.nash: NetEase fits Tom Nash's process only in part: it is profitable, cash-rich (RMB175.4B of cash and short-term investments against RMB12.6B of debt at June 2026), has expanded its operating margin every year from 18.7% (2021) to 31.8% (2025) and looks cheap on his DCF. But it is a Chinese company, which Nash tells investors to avoid, revenue grows only about 7% a year, it missed earnings estimates in two of the last four quarters, and it is not selling into a secular trend like AI.

momentum.evidence: NetEase's ADSs fell 14.63% over the 52 weeks to mid-October 2026, closing at $124.76 on October 13, 2026 (StockAnalysis).

g4.evidence: Founder William Ding has run NetEase since 1997 and insiders own about 45% of shares, and it partners with Marvel and Microsoft's Blizzard, but it lacks well-known outside investors as backers.

g6.evidence: 33 analysts rate it a 'Strong Buy' with an average price target of $162.78, about 30% above the current price (StockAnalysis, October 2026).

simple.evidence: Games were about 82% of 2025 revenue, a business of selling in-game items and games that a generalist can understand, though hit-driven economics add uncertainty.

b2.evidence: Net revenues rose every year from RMB73,667M in 2020 to RMB112,626M in 2025, and net income attributable rose from RMB12,063M to RMB33,760M.

integrity.evidence: NetEase pays out a stated share of profits as quarterly dividends (RMB13.8B paid in 2025) and buys back ADSs (US$2.0B under its program by end-2025), but founder control and the VIE structure limit minority shareholders' rights.

b6.evidence: NetEase cut back overseas studios in 2024-2025 and spun out or shrank weaker businesses, but it has also pursued side ventures such as Weiyang pig farming and Yanxuan e-commerce.

roic.evidence: Return on equity was about 20% (StockAnalysis TTM) even though NetEase holds RMB167.5B of net cash and its only borrowing is RMB12.6B of short-term loans.

fcf.evidence: In 2025 operating cash flow was RMB50,740M against net income attributable of RMB33,760M and capital spending of only RMB1,065M.

b10.evidence: Retained earnings have built a large cash pile (net cash RMB167.5B at June 2026) that earns only interest, so the market value has not grown as fast as retained profit, though dividends and buybacks return much of it.

safety.evidence: At about 17 times trailing and 12.8 times forward earnings, with net cash around 30% of the RMB-equivalent market value, the price offers some cushion but not a deep discount.

fairprice.evidence: An EV/EBIT of about 9.6 and a free-cash-flow yield of 9.3% are reasonable for a business with 64% gross margins and steady growth.

mu5.evidence: The cash-rich balance sheet makes outright failure unlikely, but Chinese regulation (such as the December 2023 draft spending rules), failed new games and US-China tensions are real ways it could disappoint.

reinvest.evidence: Games can be built at high returns, but NetEase cannot reinvest most of its cash flow (capital spending was RMB1,065M against RMB50,740M operating cash flow in 2025), so cash accumulates.

ly2.evidence: It is a stalwart: a profitable, slow-to-moderate grower (revenue up 7.0% in 2025) whose story rests on long-running franchises plus new global hits.

ly3.evidence: The trailing P/E of about 17 is well above the roughly 7% annual revenue growth analysts forecast through 2028.

runway.evidence: Consensus expects revenue to grow from RMB112.6B in 2025 to about RMB138.1B in 2028 (about 7% a year), driven by global PC and console games, which is steady rather than substantial growth.

ly7.evidence: NetEase repurchased about 22.1 million ADSs for US$2.0B by end-2025 and diluted ADS-equivalents fell from 673.5M in 2021 to 643.6M in 2025, but there is no record of open-market insider buying.

ly8.evidence: Covered by about 34 analysts, it is not overlooked, though Chinese stocks remain out of favour with many Western investors.

fi2.evidence: As older titles mature NetEase keeps launching new ones, such as Eggy Party (2022), Marvel Rivals (December 2024) and Where Winds Meet.

fi3.evidence: Its RMB17.7B of 2025 R&D produced hits such as Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet, helping gross margin rise from 53.6% in 2021 to 64.3% in 2025.

fi4.evidence: NetEase is skilled at running and monetising live-service games for decades, but its sales and marketing strength is not clearly better than Tencent's, which controls WeChat distribution.

longterm.evidence: Ding has run franchises such as Fantasy Westward Journey since 2001 and invests in multi-year original projects, favouring evergreen games over short-term launches.

gr1.evidence: It had 2025 revenue of RMB112.6B and a market value of about US$81B in October 2026.

ni10.evidence: NetEase reported positive net income attributable every year from 2016 to 2025, ending with RMB33,760M in 2025.

gr4.evidence: NetEase paid a one-off dividend in 2012 and no dividends in 2013-2015 according to its 2015 20-F, so it lacks a 20-year unbroken record.

eps10.evidence: Diluted EPS rose from RMB50.94 per old ADS in 2015 (RMB10.19 per current ADS after the 2020 ratio change) to RMB52.42 per ADS in 2025.

gr6.evidence: The market value of about RMB551B is roughly 17.8 times 2023-2025 average net income attributable of about RMB30.96B, above Graham's 15.

gr7.evidence: P/E of 16.97 times P/B of 3.22 gives about 54.6, well above 22.5 (StockAnalysis, October 2026).

th1.evidence: Its game technology and know-how are excellent but not ten times better than Tencent's or miHoYo's, which also produce global hits.

timing.evidence: The shift toward global PC and console play suits titles like Marvel Rivals, but China's game market grows slowly and licence approvals remain policy-driven.

th3.evidence: NetEase dominated China's early PC MMORPG niche with Westward Journey games from 2001 and expanded to mobile and global titles, but in its broad market it is number two to Tencent.

team.evidence: Founder William Ding has led NetEase since 1997 (CEO since 2005), building it into China's second-largest game company with operating profit of RMB35.8B in 2025.

th5.evidence: NetEase runs its own launchers and has a large player base, but it relies on app stores, Steam and consoles for distribution, unlike Tencent with WeChat.

durable.evidence: Franchises like Fantasy Westward Journey have lasted over 20 years, but game tastes change and each new title must win players.

th7.evidence: Its strategy of global original IP is shared by Tencent, miHoYo and others, so it is not a unique opportunity.

trend.evidence: NetEase uses AI in games and Youdao but is not a leading beneficiary of AI or cloud computing; its growth rests on games.

dr1.evidence: Q2 2026 operating profit rose 33.4% year on year to RMB12,089M, but net income attributable fell 18.8% because of investment losses.

dr2.evidence: Results in 18-24 months depend on how its new-game pipeline performs, which is hard to judge in advance.

dr4.evidence: Chinese monetary easing helps sentiment toward Chinese stocks, but weak Chinese consumer spending and US-China tensions are headwinds.

dr6.evidence: New game launches and expansions (such as further Marvel Rivals seasons and Where Winds Meet updates), licence approvals and continued buybacks could lift results.

dr7.evidence: Hit-driven revenue and Chinese policy and ADR risks make it hard to justify a large concentrated position.

gm.evidence: Gross margin was 64.3% in 2025 (RMB72,402M on RMB112,626M revenue), up from 53.6% in 2021.

fcfyield.evidence: Free-cash-flow yield is about 9.3% (P/FCF of 10.72, StockAnalysis October 2026), attractive for its quality.

gb2.evidence: EV/EBIT is about 9.58, an operating earnings yield of about 10% on enterprise value.

pa2.evidence: Chinese-stock discounts and investment losses in Q2 2026 are temporary-looking setbacks, but the shares' weakness is not a deep crisis.

pa4.evidence: With net cash of RMB167.5B and steady profits, the chance of permanent loss from business failure is small, though ADR and policy risks exist.

wo1.evidence: NetEase is a games company and is not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or multiomic sequencing.

wo2.evidence: Game production costs are rising, not falling, as titles grow larger.

wo3.evidence: It does not combine several of ARK's innovation platforms.

wo4.evidence: The global games market grows in single digits, so its addressable market will not be many times larger in five years.

ac3.evidence: Digital game revenue does not depend on commodity prices, and with net cash its earnings are not hurt by higher interest rates.

ns1.evidence: Free-to-play pricing gives players much content free, but NetEase has not visibly passed scale savings to customers as a deliberate strategy.

ns4.evidence: Global hits could make it stronger in 10-20 years, but its position depends on future hits and Chinese regulation.

va2.evidence: Its games entertain hundreds of millions of people but do not solve a large, painful problem.

tn1.evidence: NetEase sells games and entertainment, not infrastructure for AI, energy or robotics; AI is used in its games and Youdao but is not what it is built for.

tn2.evidence: The market still prices it as a Chinese mobile-game company, while it is becoming a global PC and console publisher with hits such as Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet, though that shift is already widely discussed.

tn3.evidence: NetEase is a Chinese company (VIE structure, ADSs on NASDAQ), one of Nash's zones to avoid, even though it is large and not a startup.

tn4.evidence: It passes all three: revenue rose every year from RMB87,606M (2021) to RMB112,626M (2025), net income was RMB33,760M in 2025, and cash and short-term investments of RMB175,393M far exceeded RMB12,604M of debt at June 30, 2026.

tn5.evidence: Free cash flow was positive in each quarter from Q1 2025 to Q1 2026 (RMB11,653M, RMB10,672M, RMB12,664M, RMB14,686M and RMB13,421M per StockAnalysis), and cash stayed above RMB170B against debt of about RMB11-13B.

tn6.evidence: Revenue grew 6.96% in 2025 (RMB105,295M to RMB112,626M) and 7.94% in Q2 2026, below Nash's 10% bar; consensus expects about 7% in 2026.

tn7.evidence: 2025 revenue growth of 6.96% plus a free-cash-flow margin of 44.11% (RMB49,674M on RMB112,626M) gives about 51, well above 40.

tn8.evidence: In 2025 revenue rose 6.96% while total operating costs (revenue minus operating income) rose only 1.4%, from RMB75,711M to RMB76,791M.

tn9.evidence: It fails two instant kills: revenue growth below 10% (6.96% in 2025) and two earnings-per-ADS misses in the last four quarters (Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 per Investing.com); other tests pass (market cap about $81B, net cash, short interest 0.85%, operating margin 35.2%, founded 1997).

tn10.evidence: Chinese game regulation (licence approvals, minors' playtime limits, the December 2023 draft spending rules) and US-China ADR delisting risk are major regulatory threats.

tn11.evidence: NetEase provides online games and entertainment that help hundreds of millions of players have fun with friends, and charges mainly through in-game purchases; players choose it for long-supported, high-quality titles such as Fantasy Westward Journey and Marvel Rivals.

tn13.evidence: Total 75 (borderline): cash vs debt 10, revenue growth 0 (6.3% TTM), operating margin 10 (35.2%), short interest 10 (0.85%), institutional ownership 5 (34.4%), revenue faster than expenses 10, 5-year return 0 (about +19% vs +56% for SPY, real total returns), moat 5, CEO 10, pricing power 5, secular trend 0, culture 5, talent 5.

tn14.evidence: From 2021 to 2025 revenue rose every year, operating margin expanded every year (18.7%, 20.3%, 26.8%, 28.1%, 31.8%), free cash flow rose every year (RMB23.3B to RMB49.7B) and cash far exceeded debt throughout.

tn15.evidence: At June 30, 2026 interest coverage was about 123x (StockAnalysis), assets of RMB232,208M were about 3.8x liabilities of RMB60,646M even excluding goodwill, the current ratio was 3.45, and liabilities were only 0.35x equity.

tn20.evidence: Per Investing.com, NetEase missed EPS estimates in Q4 2025 (RMB10.95 vs 14.12) and Q2 2026 (RMB12.02 vs 15.54) while beating in Q1 2026 and Q3 2025, so beats are not consistent.

tn21.evidence: No red flags found: founder-CEO with no co-CEO, no acquisition spree, no auditor change or accounting concerns, margins rising every year and no inventory build-up; the main concerns are regulatory rather than governance flags.

tn22.evidence: It has RMB112.6B of revenue, strong profits, buys back shares rather than issuing them, and is not a hype stock.

tn24.evidence: With enterprise value of about $57.9B (about RMB393B) against trailing free cash flow of about $7.6B, a DCF at 10-12% with a 37.5% FCF margin implies revenue shrinking by roughly 4-10% a year, well below the 6-7% growth it is delivering.

tn26.evidence: Forward P/E of 12.8 is low for a mature, 64%-gross-margin company, but with consensus EPS growth of 6.2% for 2026 and 16.0% for 2027 the PEG is about 0.8-2.1, so it passes PEG of 1 only on the 2027 estimate.
